System Architecture

Four stages.
One seamless experience.

SPANDANA is built on a tight hardware-to-AI pipeline designed specifically for low-latency feedback. From raw IMU capture to edge inference, every step is optimized for the athlete.

Note

This demo utilizes a simulated sensor feed mirroring the physics of real IMU output. Backend integration is pending post-hackathon phase.

01

IMU Hardware

A 6-DOF IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope) worn on the torso captures raw motion data at 10 Hz. Low-latency BLE transmission sends each frame to the companion app.

MPU-6050Bluetooth LE10 Hz polling
02

Dataset Assembly

Multiple athletes perform exercises while IMU data is collected and frame-by-frame labelled by certified trainers. This dataset trains the core classification model.

Multi-user datasetExpert annotationAugmentation pipeline
03

Edge Inference

A lightweight time-series classification model (1D-CNN) distinguishes good form from common errors across a configurable angle threshold. Exported to TF Lite.

1D-CNNTensorFlow LiteQuantised for edge
04

Real-time Feedback

Each inference frame triggers a form-status output with a human-readable tip. Sub-50 ms latency ensures athletes can act on feedback mid-rep.

Socket.io stream<50 ms latencyHaptic cues
